rows.title: sendToClaude() cannot reach a Claude Code session in a remote container
rows.summary: Measured 2026-09-21 (S281): the comments capability's sendToClaude() reports no_session from a remote-container Claude Code session EVEN WITH a live, confirmed artifact watch. The watch was re-registered and listed at 13:42:11Z, Sam pressed Complete at 13:43:24Z, the page still reported 'no session is listening' and replies/done carried sent:false. A lapsed watch was a real condition and was NOT the cause. Do not re-diagnose consent or permissions. It works from a claude.ai chat session. The reliable path: replies/done is a durable record needing nothing alive at press time, so arm a send_later that reads it and compares its at.

rows.title: An adjudication second look must never see the verdict it checks
rows.summary: The Trail Crew playbook requires an adversarial skeptic on every merge proposal, and its working version re-derived the numbers rather than re-reading the claim. Handing a model its own conclusion and asking it to critique invites agreement, and the failure is SILENT: a rubber-stamping skeptic produces a clean report with a high confirmation rate, indistinguishable from a pass that worked. kb/_jev_adjudicate.py asks the NEGATIVE question from the same evidence in a separate call with the first answer withheld. A refuted proposal routes to the curator however confident the first look was; the gate is symmetric so a 0.5 hedge is not a refutation; the second call is spent only above the gate. tests/jev_adjudicate_test.py asserts the skeptic call does not contain the first verdict.

rows.title: An opt-out decision sheet must record who ruled and who let it ride
rows.summary: Sam, 2026-09-21: 'set the decision button for each item to your recommended and I will change only if needed -- opt-out approach'. A pre-selected chip is indistinguishable from an answered one, so a sheet abandoned at item 30 hands over verdicts for 31-51 nobody read. They are still handed over -- that is what opt-out IS -- but never as his: no stored reply means the item carries the proposal, a stored reply is always by:'sam', and Complete commits the rest by:'default'. CONSEQUENCE: any matcher calibration must score against by:'sam' rows only; an as-proposed row measures the default, never the model.
rows.verified_by: Sam Lee (2026-09-21), recorded by SkyAnvil S281

rows.title: Jev adjudication lives in one module for CSR, CER and CCRR; CCR is not wired
rows.summary: kb/_jev_adjudicate.py is the single Jev magic half. The method+magic pattern is the repo's own (playbook-trail-crew-method-magic-audit, run twice 2026-07-10 on CER then CSR); every reference owns a METHOD half and what differs is the magic one, and the playbook records that the CCR has never had a magic half at scale. CCRR blocking is IMPORTED from _typesafe_cr_trial.build_pairs(), never reimplemented. Triage measured 2026-09-21: CER 239 findings -> 59 worth a call (180 mechanical), CSR 185 -> 143, CCRR 55 anchored pairs. The 2026-09-20 receipt's 51 pairs are ALL still present (reconciled, none lost); the 4 new pairs sit under the community relations anchor. CCR deliberately not wired: its method half emits Trust Cards rather than findings. Run via typesafe-smoke.yml -- typesafe.ai is egress-blocked from the sandbox. It SUGGESTS and writes nothing.
